In Chelsea Park, West Vancouver, the 55+ homes you can buy are Nearest, outside the sub-area and Nearest, outside the sub-area (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is rental and retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Chelsea Park
Nearest, outside the sub-area — Tudor Gardens, 843 22nd Street (Dundarave, below/south-west)

Built 1992. Building sources record age restrictions, pets not allowed and rentals not allowed, and a listing states the rule plainly: "55+ age restriction, no pets," with a large activity room, library and courtyard, one block from the seawall and across from the West Vancouver Community Centre. The "rentals not allowed" line in older building data cannot stand as a long-term rental ban under current BC law —.
Nearest, outside the sub-area — Westview Terrace, 1390 Duchess Avenue (Ambleside, below/east)

A North Shore realty guide lists it among West Vancouver buildings that "all have a 55+ bylaw," and a current listing describes "a quiet, well-kept 25-unit concrete building (55+)" two blocks to Ambleside village, the seawall and the beach. Treat the bylaw as listing/guide-stated and confirm it in the strata documents.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Chelsea Park (not for sale)

items.t: Nearest, outside the sub-area — the Kiwanis cluster on 21st Street / Gordon Avenue (Ambleside): Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society provides independent living apartments at below-market rates for adults 55+ on the North Shore. Its West Vancouver buildings are Kiwanis Manor, 959 21st Street (labelled "55+ • WEST VANCOUVER" by the society; independent living, applications year-round, North Shore residents preferred, no pets), The Court, 2151 Gordon Avenue, The Cypress, 999 21st Street, and The Terrace, 975 21st Street. Society eligibility in its application material: capable of living independently, non-smoker, 55 or older, with income and asset limits updated annually against BC Housing's low-and-moderate income limits. Rental only — nothing to buy.

Amica West Vancouver — 659 Clyde Avenue: Registered assisted living, operator Amica West Vancouver Inc.; Amica describes private independent-living and assisted-living suites plus licensed residential care at this address.

Amica Lions Gate — Keith Road: Registered assisted living, class SN. The Registry's crawled listings give the address two ways — 727 Keith Road and 701-721 Keith Road — while the operator's own page gives 701-727 Keith Road; use the operator's range and treat the exact civic range as a minor source conflict. Amica states it offers independent living, assisted living, long-term care, memory care and respite here, and notes many residents come from the West Vancouver communities of Ambleside, Dundarave and British Properties — the British Properties reference is the closest any residence source comes to this pocket.

Hollyburn House — 2095 Marine Drive: Registered assisted living, class SN, now marketed by Cogir as Venvi Hollyburn House; the operator lists independent living, assisted living, residential care, short-term and respite stays, across from the Seniors' Activity Centre and library, between Ambleside and Dundarave.

Inglewood Care Centre — 725 Inglewood Avenue: Long-term care, not a purchase: opened 1979, operated by Baptist Housing Society (not for profit), 230 publicly funded beds as of March 31, 2025 per the BC Seniors Advocate's facility file. Access is through Vancouver Coastal Health assessment.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Chelsea Park

items.t: Chelsea Park is a small residential pocket in the District of West Vancouver at the south edge of the British Properties, above Wentworth Avenue and Queens Avenue and south of Highway 1. The District does not use "Chelsea Park" as an official neighbourhood or planning-area name — NOT CONFIRMED as a District name; what District sources show is the street cluster itself: Chelsea Court, Chelsea Place and Chelsea Close around Chairlift Road, Skilift Place and Bramwell Road, plus a District pump house at 2600 Chelsea Court. Boundaries are UNVERIFIED as an official line.
Nearby areas: the British Properties (north), Whitby Estates and Chartwell (north-east), Dundarave (south-west, below) and Altamont (west).

Housing form: single-family homes in the RS zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 (RS2, RS3, RS5 and RS7 all appear in District material for this area). No named condo building or townhome complex inside Chelsea Park is confirmed on an official or developer source —.
The pocket's one named place is a park, not housing: Chairlift Park, on the Chelsea Close streets, listed in the District Parks Master Plan as RS7 and Dedicated.

Schools: no SD45 school is physically inside Chelsea Park. SD45 catchments are address-based, and the SD45 School Locator run for the sample address 2600 Chelsea Court returned NO RESULT — the locator's listed ranges for Chelsea Court are even 2620–2748 and odd 2611–2757, and 2600 falls outside both — so the catchment for Chelsea Park addresses is UNVERIFIED; run the exact listing address. Nearby: Westcot Elementary (K–7), described by SD45 as at the foot of the British Properties, and Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue in Dundarave. SD45 has no middle tier (K–7 elementary, 8–12 secondary).

Transit: TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, runs via Skilift Road, Folkestone Way and Chippendale Road at the west edge of the pocket; route 251 (Queens / Park Royal) runs on Queens Avenue below the area to Park Royal.

Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, is the Vancouver Coastal Health hospital serving the North Shore including West Vancouver; the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade, North Vancouver.

Shopping and services are downhill: Park Royal, at Marine Drive and Taylor Way, is recognized in the OCP as the regional shopping centre; the District's Seniors' Activity Centre is at 695 21st Street in Ambleside, across from Hollyburn House. Shopping or grocery inside Chelsea Park itself: UNVERIFIED (none confirmed).

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Chelsea Park

items.t: District zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: Chelsea Park houses sit in the RS single-family zones (RS2, RS3, RS5 and RS7 appear in District material here); Section 200 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with secondary suites and detached secondary suites (coach houses) among the permitted uses addressed in District building-permit guidance. The bylaw's ground-oriented rules allow 4 dwellings per lot, or 6 if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop — the stay-in-place route (suite for a caregiver or family) instead of a 55+ move.

Community plan: the District of West Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, covers Chelsea Park; no Chelsea Park-specific local area plan is confirmed. On December 1, 2025, Council adopted OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025, aligning the OCP with the 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report.

District seniors-housing policy context: the District's own Canada Community-Building Fund reporting states seniors were about one in five West Vancouver residents in 2001 and nearly one in three in 2021, with a median age of 51 in 2021, and that the 2018 OCP's policies include expanding housing choice in existing neighbourhoods; the Ambleside planning work expressly contemplates "new non-market rental, market rental, rent-to-own, co-op, seniors, strata apartment, and strata 'missing-middle' housing" — in Ambleside, where the existing seniors stock already sits, not in pockets like Chelsea Park.

British Properties context: the District's history page states a British group led by the Guinness family purchased most of the Upper Lands and began to build the British Properties, and built the Lions Gate Bridge — Chelsea Park sits at the south edge of those lands, which is why its comparables and marketing often sit under British Properties labels. Whether any British Properties building scheme or covenant step applies to a specific Chelsea street is UNCONFIRMED — check title per lot.

Hazard permits: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface; a creek, slope or foreshore fact specific to Chelsea Park is UNVERIFIED.

Taxes: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. At Chelsea Park price points the Province's additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027. Water and sewer are metered and billed quarterly; the District's water report lists a pump house at 2600 Chelsea Court, confirming District water service on the street.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chelsea Park

items.t: "Chelsea Park" is not a District neighbourhood name at all — the District's own material shows only the street cluster (Chelsea Court/Place/Close, Chairlift Road, Skilift Place, Bramwell Road) and a pump house at 2600 Chelsea Court. Comparable sales and even school-locator ranges may sit under British Properties or Chartwell labels, so a comp set built only on the "Chelsea Park" name will be thin and possibly wrong.

The school locator literally has a hole on Chelsea Court: its listed ranges start at 2620 (even) and 2611 (odd), so an address like the District's own pump house at 2600 returns no catchment result. Any listing that states a Chelsea Park catchment without an address-level locator run is asserting something the tool itself did not confirm.

The whole District has only three buildings a North Shore guide lists as 55+-bylaw strata — Westview Terrace (1390 Duchess Ave), Tudor Gardens (843 22nd St) and Lincoln Gardens (address not stated on the guide page — UNCONFIRMED here) — all down the hill in Ambleside/Dundarave. For a pocket this small, "55+ in Chelsea Park" as a page promise would be empty; the honest product is the house-plus-suite route or the downhill buildings.

The one residence that name-checks this end of the District: Amica Lions Gate's own page says many of its residents come from the West Vancouver communities of Ambleside, Dundarave and British Properties — Chelsea Park sits at the British Properties' south edge, so that residence is where neighbours from these streets have actually gone, per the operator.

The District's big seniors build is the Inglewood redevelopment, in Ambleside: on September 21, 2026, Council approved the two-phase redevelopment of Inglewood Care Centre (725 Inglewood Ave) — Phase 1, a 364-bed publicly funded long-term care facility; Phase 2, 200 independent-living units and 161 seniors rental housing units. The District does not handle tenant placement; Baptist Housing does.

Kiwanis Manor carries two descriptions in two sources — independent 55+ rental on the society's site, registered assisted living in BC's Assisted Living Registry under a partnership name. Confirm which product it actually offers before describing it to a client.

The District's seniors services are concentrated exactly where the seniors housing is: the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street — 55+ programs, Garden Side Bistro, SACS on 21st shop, rehabilitation programs and a shuttle bus — sits across from Hollyburn House and a block from the Kiwanis 21st Street cluster. A Chelsea Park senior who moves downhill joins that cluster; one who stays uses it by car or shuttle.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Chelsea Park?
faq.a: None inside the pocket — there is no verified strata of any kind in Chelsea Park, let alone a 55+ one; the housing is freehold detached houses on Chelsea Court, Chelsea Place, Chelsea Close, Chairlift Road and Skilift Place. The nearest verified 55+ ownership buildings are downhill: Tudor Gardens, 843 22nd St (Dundarave), and Westview Terrace, 1390 Duchess Ave (Ambleside).

faq.q: Is there a 55+ rental building near Chelsea Park?
faq.a: Yes, in Ambleside: the Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society's West Vancouver buildings (Kiwanis Manor, 959 21st St; The Court, 2151 Gordon Ave; The Cypress, 999 21st St; The Terrace, 975 21st St) are independent-living rentals for 55+, below-market, with income/asset eligibility, preference for North Shore residents, and no pets. Rental only — nothing to buy.

faq.q: If I stay in my Chelsea Park house, can I add a suite or coach house?
faq.a: That is the route the zoning contemplates: secondary suite and detached secondary suite (coach house) applications are addressed in District building-permit guidance for the RS zones, and the ground-oriented rules allow up to 4 dwellings per lot (6 within 400 m of a prescribed bus stop), subject to the lot's confirmed zone on the District Zoning Map and the wildfire/watercourse permit checks.

faq.q: Which school catchment is a Chelsea Park house in?
faq.a: UNVERIFIED — do not take it from the street name or from proximity. The SD45 locator returned no result for the sample address 2600 Chelsea Court because it falls outside the locator's listed ranges for the street (even 2620–2748, odd 2611–2757); run the exact listing address. Westcot Elementary at the foot of the British Properties is nearby, but proximity is not catchment.

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the nearest 55+ options?
faq.a: Tudor Gardens is recorded as no pets, and Kiwanis seniors communities do not permit pets; Westview Terrace's pet position is UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked — confirm in the specific building's bylaws/Form B.

faq.q: Where is the hospital, and what if I need care later?
faq.a: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore including West Vancouver. The in-District ladder is downhill in Ambleside: registered assisted living at Amica West Vancouver (659 Clyde Ave), Amica Lions Gate (Keith Rd) and Hollyburn House (2095 Marine Dr), then long-term care at Inglewood Care Centre (725 Inglewood Ave, 230 publicly funded beds).

faq.q: What transit can a Chelsea Park senior actually use?
faq.a: The pocket's own service is the 256 community shuttle via Skilift Road to Park Royal, with the 251 on Queens Avenue below — useful for a Park Royal trip, but most Chelsea Park households drive for daily trips. The Seniors' Activity Centre in Ambleside also runs a seniors' shuttle bus.
